actor: Open-weights release engineer, frontier joint-modality generative model lab
job: Assembling the promised open Dev checkpoint from a jointly trained backbone, deciding per head which modalities the published artifact carries.
outcome: A downloadable Dev checkpoint carrying image, video and audio generation only, with the action-conditioning path absent or disabled.
motivation: A joint backbone makes modality release checkpoint surgery, so shipping the trunk alone still satisfies the letter of the open-weights commitment.

task.who: Model release engineering and checkpoint packaging team
task.what: Strip the action head from the published Dev checkpoint
task.where: Checkpoint export pipeline and public model-weight distribution repository
task.why: Ship an open artifact without opening actuation weights
task.how: Per-head checkpoint surgery on the shared multimodal trunk

actor: Licensing counsel for a robotics foundation-model collaboration partner
job: Negotiating release consent for jointly developed video-action weights that already carry a named industrial deployment on a partner's factory floor.
outcome: A licensing position that excludes jointly owned action weights from any public, unconditioned open-weights release.
motivation: Action capability came out of the collaboration, not one lab alone, so opening it needs a consent an image model never needed.

task.who: Partner-side IP and collaboration contracts counsel
task.what: Review release consent for co-developed action weights
task.where: Joint development agreement and IP consent review process
task.why: Co-owned actuation weights need partner consent to publish
task.how: Joint development agreement consent and field-of-use clauses

actor: Early-access program manager for a gated robot-action model variant
job: Running per-applicant application review for the action variant instead of converting it to unconditioned public download during the promised window.
outcome: The action variant stays reachable only through approved applications, never as a checkpoint fetchable without per-applicant approval.
motivation: Application gating keeps deployment selection, embodiment support and downstream accountability with the lab, which unconditioned weight distribution would surrender.

task.who: Early-access intake, developer relations and deployment support staff
task.what: Screen and approve access applications for the action variant
task.where: Early-access application queue and gated model endpoint
task.why: Keep actuation capability behind per-applicant approval, not open download
task.how: Application intake, approval workflow, hosted early-access endpoint

actor: Robot-embodiment data lead building the manipulation adaptation recipe
job: Collecting manipulation trajectories physically per embodiment and refining the fast task-adaptation recipe layered on top of that scarce corpus.
outcome: The action head's differentiator stays in unpublished trajectory data and adaptation tooling rather than in downloadable weights.
motivation: Image and video corpora are scraped at web scale; manipulation data is collected robot by robot and is the actual moat.

task.who: Robotics data collection and adaptation research team
task.what: Collect per-embodiment trajectories and tune the adaptation recipe
task.where: Robot teleoperation rigs and industrial deployment sites
task.why: Scarce physical data, not the trunk, is the differentiator
task.how: Per-embodiment teleoperation capture and few-shot adaptation tooling

actor: Model-release risk reviewer, frontier lab policy and legal function
job: Assessing whether an openly downloadable checkpoint emitting motor commands is releasable while statutory shutdown authority over large developers is pending.
outcome: A release determination scoping the open artifact to generative modalities and excluding any head that emits robot actions.
motivation: An open image model emits pixels; an open action model emits motor commands, a categorically different liability an irrevocable release cannot recall.

task.who: Policy, safety and product legal release-review committee
task.what: Scope the open release to non-actuating modalities
task.where: Internal model-release review board and legal sign-off
task.why: Published actuation weights carry irrevocable physical-harm liability
task.how: Pre-release risk assessment against pending model-control legislation
